name: Mechanical Engineering
boundaries: Mechanical Engineering: fundamental discoveries and enabling technologies within this field. Include cross-field consequences where the central advance belongs to this field; exclude routine incremental optimization. Use the historical breakthroughs in the prompt to calibrate revolutionary impact.

original_dispositions.reason: The retained concept includes demanding ambient machine service. The historical requirements of indefinite life and a 20–40% global reduction are unsupported.
The addition preserves the predictive goal while using uncertainty and transferable, blind testing instead of promising exact predictions for every contact.
The addition targets broad practical design capability; arbitrary infeasible specifications and provable global simplicity are not assumed.
Added in amended form. The transformative underlying opportunity is inexpensive, accessible, efficient long-duration storage. Perfect efficiency and zero loss are not necessary to that outcome.

Covered in part: these respectively address fatigue damage, reconfiguration, and stress-directed reinforcement. Their combination does not automatically repair every kind of machine damage or eliminate maintenance.

Useful isolation is already established; the historical DC-to-MHz, all-direction, perfect-isolation claim combines incompatible or unspecified conditions, including static support. A bounded low-frequency, load-bearing advance could be valuable, but the evidence reviewed here does not establish a distinct proposed capability at the selected revolutionary-impact bar. Research on practical trade-offs continues; the Song, Singh, and Karathanasopoulos 2026 record was accessible at abstract level, and the full-text fetch returned 403.

Efficient propulsors already exist, and a nominal 90% figure depends on how propulsive efficiency and operating conditions are defined. The historical fuel-saving estimates are unsupported; a specific new mechanical capability with a demonstrated transformative advantage was not established in this research.
The practical goal is transferable prediction across materially different contact regimes; a single closed-form solution for all environments is not required.

Low-loss, low-backlash transmissions already exist; exact losslessness over arbitrary distances and paths is not a physically supported requirement. The historical examples do not establish a distinct transformative capability beyond the machinery and actuation advances retained here.

Moving overconstrained mechanisms already exist. The historical claim does not identify a demonstrated missing principle or a specific capability whose achievement would independently meet the impact bar.
